“Which side do you want me on,” someone calls out from right behind where we anchor. I’m caught offguard. It’s not Mike, who has already waded on downriver and disappeared somewhere on the far shore. It’s an angler in a one-seater pontoon-style raft. She floats by as a dark apparition on the river, vague and barely legible. It is all quite mysterious and exciting—a little eerie—the fact that these mysterious people are out here under the stars on this river, my guess is probably for the same reasons.
“There’s a very real chance to catch the fish of a lifetime at night,” Longstreet says.
It’s 8:50 p.m. and I wonder if Longstreet crushing the bard on the foam mouse fly was a purely ethical move, or is it because he’s skeptical of my skills? We have fished together before, and long enough this evening to create a solid sample set of what could potentially go wrong on a muffed back cast.
“I don’t mind if you cast over me,” Longstreet says. I can hear in his voice that he is trying to be brave, probably as a matter of principal. He’s a professional, but the trust level is not quite as palpable as the pickled eggs.
Several fish that I hook into go AWOL, a term the writer John McPhee uses to describe fish that throw your hook before you can land them: Absent Without Leave. This is heartbreaking, but it also drives the negative feedback loop that I feel myself slowly falling into, as if this whole thing is some kind of gateway drug.
Tonight I am working through the nuances of the strip-set, which is, according to Longstreet, one of the keys to better hook ups while streamer fishing in the dark. Another is to keep the rod tip low to the water. “Even in the water,” Longstreet says. He patters me, “rod tip down.” This is a line management tool. This is staying in contact with the fish. Another key point is to not bury the streamer’s hook into the skull of your guide rowing the drift boat. I constantly worry about it. Afterall, you can’t see a damn thing.
“Has anyone ever buried a hook in you, Billy” I ask.
“Not yet,” Longstreet says.
More pressure.
It is odd, not being able to see anything at all except for where the dark blue night sky meets the inky outline of the rolling hills surrounding us. And the millions of stars. You can’t see your cast, or where it lands really. It is somewhere over there under the big dipper. The water is just a confusing reflection of dark silhouettes and random sources of light rippling together. But there develops this underlying notion to it all, fishing in the dark. You work mostly on muscle memory, on feel. You feel the heavy line slide through the guides and go tight against the reel as it falls onto the water. You get hints from the water of the v-shaped wake following the slow strip of the mouse, painfully slow. It is the perfect change of pace.
When these nocturnal browns take the fly at the end of your line, it does feel like a boulder on the bottom of the river for a moment, except then the boulder is vibrating, swimming away from you, diving, running, jumping and thrashing. You are fighting a fish filled with rage, and international genetics that date back to at least the nineteenth century. It is causing you to be half fearful for your life, and half fearful that you may, in fact, have the best trout of your life tight to your line. Or a ghost. You can’t see. It’s like playing a power chord. You’re going off emotion and sensation.
If it wasn’t for Longstreet, I’d probably be at home sleeping, and not ruining my life sitting in his boat on this river, drifting further down this rabbit hole of addiction. But here I am, unfortunately.
T.C. Mazar is a freelance outdoors writer and can be reached at wildlife@scrantontimes.com.

item.title: Noel Gallagher reacts to bombshell Man City charges verdict
item.description: Noel Gallagher reacted with "shock" and "sadness" to reports of Manchester City being found guilty of financial breaches, while a former chairman anticipated "drastic" penalties.
item.content:encoded:
Oasis musician Noel Gallagher has expressed his "shock" following news that Manchester City have been found guilty on almost all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules.
Reports on Friday claimed City had been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges issued by the Premier League in February 2023, allegations the club consistently denied.
Speaking on the Let Me Talk podcast, the prominent City supporter called the decision "quite sad" for fans and squad members.
"A little surprised when I heard it on the radio. Surprised because only that the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges.
"So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we've been found guilty of all but one. But really overall just quite sad really. Sad for the fans and for the players."
When asked whether the verdict alters historic moments such as Sergio Aguero's title-winning goal in 2012, Gallagher added: "Our focus as fans is always on the pitch and we know what we saw – they won it on the pitch.
"Whatever goes on in the boardroom, it's nothing to do with the supporters or the players. The players won that game and won that title on the pitch.
"Whether some of those players should have been there or not, that's nothing to do with the fans. We were there, we know what we saw.
"Does it taint it? I suppose in the eyes of everybody else in England it would, but I know what I saw and I know what I felt."
Meanwhile, former City chairman David Bernstein has admitted the club faces a "drastic" punishment if their appeal fails.
Urging swift action, Bernstein said on Times Radio: "First of all, the timing of this I think is crucial. This whole process has taken too long already.
"So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because…you've got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it's just not viable.
"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial.
"I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.
"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

item.title: OnePlus 16 Debuts Notification Lighting Amid Halted Sales
item.description: The OnePlus 16, featuring a new rear notification LED system, has been announced for 2026 amid a halt in sales for the company in North America and Europe.
item.content:encoded:
The OnePlus 16 introduces the Interstellar Lighting Effect, a rear notification LED system, as the company halts sales in North America and Europe. Rivals like Nothing and Asus also feature similar lighting.
OnePlus has unveiled the OnePlus 16, a new smartphone featuring the Interstellar Lighting Effect, as the company halts sales in North America and Europe. The announcement comes in 2026, with the phone's rear lighting system drawing comparisons to competitors like Nothing. The OnePlus 16 aims to alert users to incoming notifications through a unique three-zone lighting design on its Tomorrow's Starlight colorway.
The OnePlus 16's Interstellar Lighting Effect is designed to alert owners to incoming notifications. The glass surface includes three distinct lighting zones, each carved with specific designs. At the bottom-left corner, text reads 16 AREA. To its right, celestial coordinates point to an indeterminate location between the constellations Hydra and Monoceros. An X-marks-the-spot marker sits at the top-right corner. Previews suggest the LEDs glow only in warm, solar hues. It remains unclear what level of settings control users will have over these lights.
The OnePlus 16 is positioned as a direct competitor to Nothing, a brand founded by Carl Pei, who co-founded OnePlus. Nothing's first phone, launched in 2022, gained praise for its fashion-forward aesthetic, notably the Glyph Interface. The OnePlus 16's lighting effect mirrors this trend, sparking discussions among tech enthusiasts.
Front-facing notification LEDs were once standard on many smartphones through the mid-2010s. They were displaced as phone makers expanded screens to fill more surface area. Some manufacturers used the camera flash LED as an alternative, but this feature required users to opt in and did not catch on widely. Meanwhile, the industry shifted from LCD panels to OLED displays, which are more power-efficient. Since each pixel can turn on or off individually, always-on displays became viable for passive notifications, reducing the need for dedicated LEDs.
This confluence of developments led to the reinvention of the notification LED. Nothing has been the splashiest with its takes, but it was not the first. Asus launched its Republic of Gamers series in 2018 with customizable RGB lighting on the rear. More recently, other brands have followed suit. Nothing's Glyph LEDs have evolved over the years: starting on the Phone (1) as concentric bands of white LEDs with user-assigned pulse patterning, it morphed several times before arriving as a retro-style pixel array.
Competitors like Asus and Xiaomi have also embraced rear lighting. Xiaomi went further with its 17 Pro and Pro Max, converting the camera plateau into a full-fledged, albeit tiny, screen. This innovation shows how OEMs continue to push the envelope. The OnePlus 16's Interstellar Lighting Effect adds to this trend, though its sales halt in North America and Europe raises questions about its market impact.
As the smartphone industry evolves, lighting features may become more integrated. The OnePlus 16's launch in 2026 highlights ongoing experimentation with form and function. For now, the Interstellar Lighting Effect remains a notable addition to the OnePlus lineup, even as the company adjusts its sales strategy in key regions.

item.title: AI Trainers for OpenAI's AI Fired for Using AI to Train the AI. AI [Obvious]
item.description: An article discusses the firing of OpenAI's AI trainers for using AI to train AI, raising concerns about data integrity and AI model collapse.
item.content:encoded:
AI Trainers for OpenAI's AI Fired for Using AI to Train the AI. AI
Rookie mistake. You have to remember to tell the AI to formulate answers in a non-AI fashion.
And this is exactly why LLMs are a one way trip into a brick wall. AI needs human created content, but it's steadily poisoning that content with its own output. Once you feed it back to itself you get a decoherence of the model. Even if you don't have deliberate cases like this, it's already more and more difficult to get 'clean' input. Okay, maybe I'm the one taking crazy pills here. My background is computational linguistics not AI (and I did fark all with my linguistics degree) so it's a certainty my understanding is at best weak. But it seems to me that the more that training data gets created by AI, the less useful it becomes. So we will hit a data training wall, along with the scalability wall. The AI folks answer to get past this seems to be "and then a miracle happens". But no one seems to know what exactly that miracle is.
No, we're going to rebrand AI training AI from "model collapse" to "recursive self improvement".

item.title: Best and Worst Black Fashion at the MTV Video Music Awards Over the Years
item.description: This article reviews the best and worst Black fashion looks from previous MTV Video Music Awards ahead of the upcoming 2026 ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards are heading back to Los Angeles this Sunday, Sept. 27, and you already know the red carpet is where things can get interesting. Snoop Dogg is taking the hosting duties, with Black stars including Teyana Taylor and Tyla among the presenters.
Over the years, the VMAs red carpet has given us plenty of unforgettable fashion moments, from genuinely iconic to downright questionable. So, before this year’s stars step in front of the cameras, let’s revisit some of the good and bad looks that had us talking long after the show ended!
Best: Cardi B- 2023
You already know Cardi B was going to be at the top of our list for one of the best! She hasn’t met a red carpet look that she hasn’t slayed in a long time, and her fit at the 2023 VMAs further proves that!
Worst: Doja Cat- 2025
Between the big hair, the pattern on the dress, and the outrageous heels, we’re just not so sure we’re rocking with this look from Doja Cat at the 2025 show. Can you really blame us?
Best: Lil Nas X- 2022
Talk about drama! If you’re going to have all eyes on you on a red carpet, you might as well do like Lil Nas X at the 2022 show and give them something worth looking at!
Worst: Nicki Minaj- 2011
Nicki, we get it. You’re the queen of rap. But we can’t lie and say this look didn’t make us want to snatch the crown away from you ASAP because what even is all of this mess??
Best: GloRilla- 2024
We all love a good reference and homage, and the Left Eye one GloRilla put on for the 2024 VMAs was just too good. They almost look like kin, and we truly love to see it!
Worst: Megan Thee Stallion- 2019
Megan Thee Stallion has definitely pulled off some amazing looks in her lifetime, but unfortunately, the 2019 VMAs were not one of those. And it’s such a shame considering how wonderful her physique is!
Best: Rihanna- 2007
Sometimes the best looks are the most simple, and this hot pink, sweetheart neckline dress that Rihanna wore in 2007 after “Umbrella” put her on the map was exactly that. Who knew we were looking at a budding fashion icon in the making?
Worst: Lil’ Kim- 1999
OK, we know this one might be a hot take given how legendary this outfit is! But for someone as gorgeous as Lil’ Kim, she could’ve come a lot harder than this. The color looks great on her, though!
Best: Shenseea- 2025
From the updo to the simple jewelry that doesn’t take away from the dress, Shenseea popped out at the 2025 VMAs and showed all the girls how to look very cutesy, very sexy, and very demure all at the same time!
Worst: Summer Walker- 2025
Summer, please. This hat?? We still have questions that we probably won’t get answered. But we definitely don’t need to see this look ever again.
Best: Chloe Bailey- 2022
The best thing about Chloe Bailey’s look at the 2022 VMAs is that everything just looks cohesive and clean. The fit is good, the jewel tone is good, her loc’d ponytail is good. 10s all across the board!
Worst: Akon- 2019
There are some florals that are groundbreaking. Then, there are others like the ones on Akon’s jacket at the 2019 VMAs that should just be burned, or at the very least, thrown into somebody’s trash bin.
Worst: Ice Spice- 2025
The mix-up or mash-up of all these patterns on Ice Spice’s quilt-looking dress at the 2025 VMAs doesn’t do anything for us. She really could’ve given us something to talk about instead of something that we so desperately want to forget.

item.title: Fall-like weather expected on the Gulf Coast
item.description: The Gulf Coast is experiencing fall-like weather with lower temperatures and humidity, though temperatures and rain chances will increase mid-week.
item.content:encoded:
**FORT MYERS, Fla. —**
Fall is here, and it'll feel like it across the Gulf Coast these next few days. Lower temperatures, lower humidity and minimal rain chances are expected to stick around.
Your Gulf Coast Weather Most Accurate Forecast calls for afternoon highs to climb into the 80s.
Rain chances are minimal, and lower humidity will make it feel less muggy than usual.
On Sunday, morning lows will fall into the 60s areawide. Afternoon highs will reach into the 80s again tomorrow.
Looking ahead, rain chances and temperatures will start to increase by the middle part of the workweek.
In the tropics, Fay has weakened into a tropical depression while Tropical Storm Gonzalo maintains its strength as it moves away from the Cabo Verde Islands. Neither storm is a threat to the US.

### [‘Flat is Back’ campaign hopes to put flounder back on people’s plates](https://www.gloucestertimes.com/news/fishing_industry_news/flat-is-back-campaign-hopes-to-put-flounder-back-on-people-s-plates/article_973213d7-053c-5fb4-b629-a8b6b39d5f0b.html)
The Massachusetts Division of Marine Fisheries has launched the “Flat is Back” campaign to promote flounder, an underutilized flatfish. The initiative aims to connect fishermen's catches to consumers' plates, creating a more sustainable fisheries model. In 2023, most seafood consumed in the U.S. came from just 10 species, with flounder often overlooked. The campaign includes the Massachusetts Flounder Chef Council, which develops recipes to highlight flounder's versatility. The goal is to inspire consumers to try flounder at home, making seafood more diverse and accessible while supporting local fishermen.
